--src: Mathlib.Data.Holor
/-- `CPRankMax N x` means `x` has CP rank at most `N`, that is,
  it can be written as the sum of N holors of rank at most 1. -/
inductive CPRankMax [Mul α] [AddMonoid α] : ℕ → ∀ {ds}, Holor α ds → Prop
  | zero {ds} : CPRankMax 0 (0 : Holor α ds)
  | succ (n) {ds} (x : Holor α ds) (y : Holor α ds) :
    CPRankMax1 x → CPRankMax n y → CPRankMax (n + 1) (x + y)

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
theorem strongLT_of_strongLT_of_le (hab : a ≺ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) : a ≺ c := fun _ ↦
  (hab _).trans_le <| hbc _

--src: Mathlib.Order.BoundedOrder.Basic
theorem OrderTop.ext_top {α} {hA : PartialOrder α} (A : OrderTop α) {hB : PartialOrder α}
    (B : OrderTop α) (H : ∀ x y : α, (haveI := hA; x ≤ y) ↔ x ≤ y) :
    (@Top.top α (@OrderTop.toTop α hA.toLE A)) = (@Top.top α (@OrderTop.toTop α hB.toLE B)) := by
  cases PartialOrder.ext H
  apply top_unique
  exact @le_top _ _ A _

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
theorem type_le_iff' {α β} {r : α → α → Prop} {s : β → β → Prop} [IsWellOrder α r]
    [IsWellOrder β s] : type r ≤ type s ↔ Nonempty (r ↪r s) :=
  ⟨fun ⟨f⟩ => ⟨f⟩, fun ⟨f⟩ => ⟨f.collapse⟩⟩

--src: Mathlib.Data.List.Duplicate
/-- Property that an element `x : α` of `l : List α` can be found in the list more than once. -/
inductive Duplicate (x : α) : List α → Prop
  | cons_mem {l : List α} : x ∈ l → Duplicate x (x :: l)
  | cons_duplicate {y : α} {l : List α} : Duplicate x l → Duplicate x (y :: l)

--src: Mathlib.Order.Chain
lemma mem_iff_forall_le_or_ge : a ∈ s ↔ ∀ ⦃b⦄, b ∈ s → a ≤ b ∨ b ≤ a :=
  ⟨fun ha b => s.le_or_le ha, fun hb =>
    of_not_not fun ha =>
      Set.ne_insert_of_not_mem _ ‹_› <|
        s.maxChain.2 (s.chain_le.insert fun c hc _ => hb hc) <| Set.subset_insert _ _⟩

{ Ring₃.toAddGroup₃ with
  add_comm := by
    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

--src: Mathlib.Order.Defs.PartialOrder
/-- A preorder is a reflexive, transitive relation `≤` with `a < b` defined in the obvious way. -/
class Preorder (α : Type*) extends LE α, LT α where
  le_refl : ∀ a : α, a ≤ a
  le_trans : ∀ a b c : α, a ≤ b → b ≤ c → a ≤ c
  lt := fun a b => a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a
  lt_iff_le_not_le : ∀ a b : α, a < b ↔ a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a := by intros; rfl

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
theorem lt_iff_lt_of_le_iff_le' {β} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {a b : α} {c d : β}
    (H : a ≤ b ↔ c ≤ d) (H' : b ≤ a ↔ d ≤ c) : b < a ↔ d < c :=
  lt_iff_le_not_le.trans <| (and_congr H' (not_congr H)).trans lt_iff_le_not_le.symm

--src: Mathlib.Order.Minimal
theorem minimal_iff_forall_lt : Minimal P x ↔ P x ∧ ∀ ⦃y⦄, y < x → ¬ P y := by
  simp [Minimal, lt_iff_le_not_le, not_imp_not, imp.swap]

--src: Mathlib.Order.Antisymmetrization
@[simp]
theorem ofAntisymmetrization_lt_ofAntisymmetrization_iff {a b : Antisymmetrization α (· ≤ ·)} :
    ofAntisymmetrization (· ≤ ·) a < ofAntisymmetrization (· ≤ ·) b ↔ a < b :=
  (Quotient.outRelEmbedding _).map_rel_iff

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
theorem mk_le_mk_iff_left : (a₁, b) ≤ (a₂, b) ↔ a₁ ≤ a₂ :=

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
@[simp]
theorem mk_lt_mk : (a₁, b₁) < (a₂, b₂) ↔ a₁ < a₂ ∧ b₁ ≤ b₂ ∨ a₁ ≤ a₂ ∧ b₁ < b₂ :=
  lt_iff

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
theorem strongLT_of_strongLT_of_le (hab : a ≺ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) : a ≺ c := fun _ ↦
  (hab _).trans_le <| hbc _

--src: Mathlib.Order.Antisymmetrization
theorem AntisymmRel.image {a b : α} (h : AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) a b) {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) :

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Instances
protected theorem id_traverse {σ α} (x : σ ⊕ α) :
    Sum.traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x := by cases x <;> rfl

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Basic
/-- A traversable functor is lawful if its `traverse` satisfies a
number of additional properties.  It must send `pure : α → Id α` to `pure`,
send the composition of applicative functors to the composition of the
`traverse` of each, send each function `f` to `fun x ↦ f <$> x`, and
satisfy a naturality condition with respect to applicative
transformations. -/
class LawfulTraversable (t : Type u → Type u) [Traversable t] extends LawfulFunctor t :
    Prop where
  /-- `traverse` plays well with `pure` of the identity monad -/
  id_traverse : ∀ {α} (x : t α), traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x
  /-- `traverse` plays well with composition of applicative functors. -/
  comp_traverse :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G] {α β γ}
      (f : β → F γ) (g : α → G β) (x : t α),
      traverse (Functor.Comp.mk ∘ map f ∘ g) x = Comp.mk (map (traverse f) (traverse g x))
  /-- An axiom for `traverse` involving `pure : β → Id β`. -/
  traverse_eq_map_id : ∀ {α β} (f : α → β) (x : t α),
    traverse ((pure : β → Id β) ∘ f) x = id.mk (f <$> x)
  /-- The naturality axiom explaining how lawful traversable functors should play with
  lawful applicative functors. -/
  naturality :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G]
      (η : ApplicativeTransformation F G) {α β} (f : α → F β) (x : t α),
      η (traverse f x) = traverse (@η _ ∘ f) x

      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩

    · congr

      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

    intro a b

      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  have h₁ : g₁.one = g₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (Monoid.ext h_mul)
  let f : @MonoidHom G G g₁.toMulOneClass g₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  exact
    Group.toDivInvMonoid_injective
      (DivInvMonoid.ext h_mul
        (funext <| @MonoidHom.map_inv G G g₁ g₂.toDivisionMonoid f))

  add_comm := by
    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Defs
/-- A module is a generalization of vector spaces to a scalar semiring.
  It consists of a scalar semiring `R` and an additive monoid of "vectors" `M`,
  connected by a "scalar multiplication" operation `r • x : M`
  (where `r : R` and `x : M`) with some natural associativity and
  distributivity axioms similar to those on a ring. -/
@[ext]
class Module (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] extends
  DistribMulAction R M where
  /-- Scalar multiplication distributes over addition from the right. -/
  protected add_smul : ∀ (r s : R) (x : M), (r + s) • x = r • x + s • x
  /-- Scalar multiplication by zero gives zero. -/
  protected zero_smul : ∀ x : M, (0 : R) • x = 0

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Defs
theorem copy_eq (f : M →ₛₗ[σ] M₃) (f' : M → M₃) (h : f' = ⇑f) : f.copy f' h = f :=
  DFunLike.ext' h

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.LinearPMap
@[ext (iff := false)]
theorem ext {f g : E →ₗ.[R] F} (h : f.domain = g.domain)
    (h' : ∀ ⦃x : f.domain⦄ ⦃y : g.domain⦄ (_h : (x : E) = y), f x = g y) : f = g := by
  rcases f with ⟨f_dom, f⟩
  rcases g with ⟨g_dom, g⟩
  obtain rfl : f_dom = g_dom := h
  obtain rfl : f = g := LinearMap.ext fun x => h' rfl
  rfl

  DFunLike.coe_injective

lemma Module.ulift_injective_of_injective [Small.{v} R]
    (inj : Module.Injective R M) :
    Module.Injective R (ULift.{v'} M) := Module.Baer.injective fun I g ↦
  have ⟨g', hg'⟩ := Module.Baer.iff_injective.mpr inj I (ULift.moduleEquiv.toLinearMap ∘ₗ g)
  ⟨ULift.moduleEquiv.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ g', fun r hr ↦ ULift.ext _ _ <| hg' r hr⟩

theorem toLinearMap_injective {F : Type*} [FunLike F M M₃] [SemilinearMapClass F σ M M₃]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Injective
/--
An `R`-module `Q` is injective if and only if every injective `R`-linear map descends to a linear
map to `Q`, i.e. in the following diagram, if `f` is injective then there is an `R`-linear map
`h : Y ⟶ Q` such that `g = h ∘ f`
  ```
  X --- f ---> Y
  |
  | g
  v
  Q
  ```
-/
@[mk_iff] class Module.Injective : Prop where
  out : ∀ ⦃X Y : Type v⦄ [AddCommGroup X] [AddCommGroup Y] [Module R X] [Module R Y]
    (f : X →ₗ[R] Y) (_ : Function.Injective f) (g : X →ₗ[R] Q),
    ∃ h : Y →ₗ[R] Q, ∀ x, h (f x) = g x

      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

    ext : 1 <;> assumption
  have h₂ : inst₁.toNonAssocRing = inst₂.toNonAssocRing := by

  congr <;> solve | injection h₂ | injection h₃

    intro a b

      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Instances
protected theorem id_traverse {σ α} (x : σ ⊕ α) :
    Sum.traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x := by cases x <;> rfl

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Basic
/-- A traversable functor is lawful if its `traverse` satisfies a
number of additional properties.  It must send `pure : α → Id α` to `pure`,
send the composition of applicative functors to the composition of the
`traverse` of each, send each function `f` to `fun x ↦ f <$> x`, and
satisfy a naturality condition with respect to applicative
transformations. -/
class LawfulTraversable (t : Type u → Type u) [Traversable t] extends LawfulFunctor t :
    Prop where
  /-- `traverse` plays well with `pure` of the identity monad -/
  id_traverse : ∀ {α} (x : t α), traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x
  /-- `traverse` plays well with composition of applicative functors. -/
  comp_traverse :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G] {α β γ}
      (f : β → F γ) (g : α → G β) (x : t α),
      traverse (Functor.Comp.mk ∘ map f ∘ g) x = Comp.mk (map (traverse f) (traverse g x))
  /-- An axiom for `traverse` involving `pure : β → Id β`. -/
  traverse_eq_map_id : ∀ {α β} (f : α → β) (x : t α),
    traverse ((pure : β → Id β) ∘ f) x = id.mk (f <$> x)
  /-- The naturality axiom explaining how lawful traversable functors should play with
  lawful applicative functors. -/
  naturality :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G]
      (η : ApplicativeTransformation F G) {α β} (f : α → F β) (x : t α),
      η (traverse f x) = traverse (@η _ ∘ f) x

  functor := dual
  inverse := dual
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X
  counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X

--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.NonemptyFinLinOrd
instance : SplitEpiCategory NonemptyFinLinOrd.{u} :=
  ⟨fun {X Y} f hf => by
    have H : ∀ y : Y, Nonempty (f ⁻¹' {y}) := by
      rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hf
      intro y
      exact Nonempty.intro ⟨(hf y).choose, (hf y).choose_spec⟩
    let φ : Y → X := fun y => (H y).some.1
    have hφ : ∀ y : Y, f (φ y) = y := fun y => (H y).some.2
    refine IsSplitEpi.mk' ⟨⟨φ, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    swap
    · ext b
      apply hφ
    · intro a b
      contrapose
      intro h
      simp only [not_le] at h ⊢
      suffices b ≤ a by
        apply lt_of_le_of_ne this
        rintro rfl
        exfalso
        simp at h
      have H : f (φ b) ≤ f (φ a) := f.monotone (le_of_lt h)
      simpa only [hφ] using H⟩

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

--src: Mathlib.Order.Defs.PartialOrder
/-- A partial order is a reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric relation `≤`. -/
class PartialOrder (α : Type*) extends Preorder α where
  le_antisymm : ∀ a b : α, a ≤ b → b ≤ a → a = b

--src: Mathlib.Order.Basic
theorem ge_antisymm : a ≤ b → b ≤ a → b = a :=
  flip le_antisymm

--src: Mathlib.Order.RelClasses

{ Ring₃.toAddGroup₃ with

    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]

      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

{ Ring₃.toAddGroup₃ with
  add_comm := by
    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

{ Ring₃.toAddGroup₃ with
  add_comm := by
    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Basic
/-- A traversable functor is lawful if its `traverse` satisfies a
number of additional properties.  It must send `pure : α → Id α` to `pure`,
send the composition of applicative functors to the composition of the
`traverse` of each, send each function `f` to `fun x ↦ f <$> x`, and
satisfy a naturality condition with respect to applicative
transformations. -/
class LawfulTraversable (t : Type u → Type u) [Traversable t] extends LawfulFunctor t :
    Prop where
  /-- `traverse` plays well with `pure` of the identity monad -/
  id_traverse : ∀ {α} (x : t α), traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x
  /-- `traverse` plays well with composition of applicative functors. -/
  comp_traverse :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G] {α β γ}
      (f : β → F γ) (g : α → G β) (x : t α),
      traverse (Functor.Comp.mk ∘ map f ∘ g) x = Comp.mk (map (traverse f) (traverse g x))
  /-- An axiom for `traverse` involving `pure : β → Id β`. -/
  traverse_eq_map_id : ∀ {α β} (f : α → β) (x : t α),
    traverse ((pure : β → Id β) ∘ f) x = id.mk (f <$> x)
  /-- The naturality axiom explaining how lawful traversable functors should play with
  lawful applicative functors. -/
  naturality :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G]
      (η : ApplicativeTransformation F G) {α β} (f : α → F β) (x : t α),
      η (traverse f x) = traverse (@η _ ∘ f) x

/-- The smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` is contained in any
    congruence relation containing `r`. -/
@[to_additive addConGen_le "The smallest additive congruence relation containing a binary
relation `r` is contained in any additive congruence relation containing `r`."]
theorem conGen_le {r : M → M → Prop} {c : Con M} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → c x y) :
    conGen r ≤ c := by rw [conGen_eq]; exact sInf_le h

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the smallest congruence relation
    containing `s` contains the smallest congruence relation containing `r`. -/
@[to_additive addConGen_mono "Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the
smallest additive congruence relation containing `s` contains the smallest additive congruence
relation containing `r`."]
theorem conGen_mono {r s : M → M → Prop} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → s x y) : conGen r ≤ conGen s :=
  conGen_le fun x y hr => ConGen.Rel.of _ _ <| h x y hr

/-- A `SemilatticeInf` is a meet-semilattice, that is, a partial order

  /-- The infimum is a lower bound on the second argument -/

  protected le_inf : ∀ a b c : α, a ≤ b → a ≤ c → a ≤ inf b c

theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩

    · congr

{ Ring₃.toAddGroup₃ with
  add_comm := by
    intro a b
    have : a + (a + b + b) = a + (b + a + b) := calc
      a + (a + b + b) = (a + a) + (b + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃, add_assoc₃]
      _ = (1 * a + 1 * a) + (1 * b + 1 * b) := by simp
      _ = (1 + 1) * a + (1 + 1) * b := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (1 + 1) * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.left_distrib]
      _ = 1 * (a + b) + 1 * (a + b) := by simp [Ring₃.right_distrib]
      _ = (a + b) + (a + b) := by simp
      _ = a + (b + a + b) := by simp [add_assoc₃]
    exact add_right_cancel₃ (add_left_cancel₃ this) }

/-- A preorder is a reflexive, transitive relation `≤` with `a < b` defined in the obvious way. -/
class Preorder (α : Type*) extends LE α, LT α where
  le_refl : ∀ a : α, a ≤ a

  lt := fun a b => a ≤ b ∧ ¬b ≤ a

theorem Monotone.exists {P : β → α → Prop} (hP : ∀ x, Monotone (P x)) :

--src: Mathlib.Order.Lattice
/-- A `SemilatticeInf` is a meet-semilattice, that is, a partial order
  with a meet (a.k.a. glb / greatest lower bound, inf / infimum) operation
  `⊓` which is the greatest element smaller than both factors. -/
class SemilatticeInf (α : Type u) extends PartialOrder α where
  /-- The binary infimum, used to derive `Min α` -/
  inf : α → α → α
  /-- The infimum is a lower bound on the first argument -/
  protected inf_le_left : ∀ a b : α, inf a b ≤ a
  /-- The infimum is a lower bound on the second argument -/
  protected inf_le_right : ∀ a b : α, inf a b ≤ b
  /-- The infimum is the *greatest* lower bound -/
  protected le_inf : ∀ a b c : α, a ≤ b → a ≤ c → a ≤ inf b c

theorem conGen_mono {r s : M → M → Prop} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → s x y) : conGen r ≤ conGen s :=

/-- The smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` is contained in any
    congruence relation containing `r`. -/
@[to_additive addConGen_le "The smallest additive congruence relation containing a binary
relation `r` is contained in any additive congruence relation containing `r`."]
theorem conGen_le {r : M → M → Prop} {c : Con M} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → c x y) :
    conGen r ≤ c := by rw [conGen_eq]; exact sInf_le h

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the smallest congruence relation
    containing `s` contains the smallest congruence relation containing `r`. -/
@[to_additive addConGen_mono "Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the
smallest additive congruence relation containing `s` contains the smallest additive congruence
relation containing `r`."]
theorem conGen_mono {r s : M → M → Prop} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → s x y) : conGen r ≤ conGen s :=
  conGen_le fun x y hr => ConGen.Rel.of _ _ <| h x y hr

/-- Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the smallest congruence relation
    containing `s` contains the smallest congruence relation containing `r`. -/

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.AddChar
/-- `AddChar A M` is the type of maps `A → M`, for `A` an additive monoid and `M` a multiplicative
monoid, which intertwine addition in `A` with multiplication in `M`.
We only put the typeclasses needed for the definition, although in practice we are usually
interested in much more specific cases (e.g. when `A` is a group and `M` a commutative ring).
 -/
structure AddChar where
  /-- The underlying function.
  Do not use this function directly. Instead use the coercion coming from the `FunLike`
  instance. -/
  toFun : A → M
  /-- The function maps `0` to `1`.
  Do not use this directly. Instead use `AddChar.map_zero_eq_one`. -/
  map_zero_eq_one' : toFun 0 = 1
  /-- The function maps addition in `A` to multiplication in `M`.
  Do not use this directly. Instead use `AddChar.map_add_eq_mul`. -/
  map_add_eq_mul' : ∀ a b : A, toFun (a + b) = toFun a * toFun b

/-- Given an arbitrary relation `r` on a ring, we strengthen it to a relation `Rel r`,
such that the equivalence relation generated by `Rel r` has `x ~ y` if and only if
`x - y` is in the ideal generated by elements `a - b` such that `r a b`.
-/
inductive Rel (r : R → R → Prop) : R → R → Prop
  | of ⦃x y : R⦄ (h : r x y) : Rel r x y
  | add_left ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r a b → Rel r (a + c) (b + c)
  | mul_left ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r a b → Rel r (a * c) (b * c)
  | mul_right ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r b c → Rel r (a * b) (a * c)

    (h_mul : local_hMul[R, inst₁] = local_hMul[R, inst₂]) :

    ext : 1 <;> assumption
  have h₂ : inst₁.toNonAssocRing = inst₂.toNonAssocRing := by
    ext : 1 <;> assumption
  /- We prove that the `SubNegMonoid`s are equal because they are one
  field away from `Sub` and `Neg`, enabling use of `injection`. -/

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.RingQuot
/-- Given an arbitrary relation `r` on a ring, we strengthen it to a relation `Rel r`,
such that the equivalence relation generated by `Rel r` has `x ~ y` if and only if
`x - y` is in the ideal generated by elements `a - b` such that `r a b`.
-/
inductive Rel (r : R → R → Prop) : R → R → Prop
  | of ⦃x y : R⦄ (h : r x y) : Rel r x y
  | add_left ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r a b → Rel r (a + c) (b + c)
  | mul_left ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r a b → Rel r (a * c) (b * c)
  | mul_right ⦃a b c⦄ : Rel r b c → Rel r (a * b) (a * c)

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  have h₁ : g₁.one = g₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (Monoid.ext h_mul)
  let f : @MonoidHom G G g₁.toMulOneClass g₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  exact
    Group.toDivInvMonoid_injective
      (DivInvMonoid.ext h_mul
        (funext <| @MonoidHom.map_inv G G g₁ g₂.toDivisionMonoid f))

theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

/-- A `Group` is a `Monoid` with an operation `⁻¹` satisfying `a⁻¹ * a = 1`.
There is also a division operation `/` such that `a / b = a * b⁻¹`,
with a default so that `a / b = a * b⁻¹` holds by definition.
Use `Group.ofLeftAxioms` or `Group.ofRightAxioms` to define a group structure
on a type with the minimum proof obligations.
-/

  protected inv_mul_cancel : ∀ a : G, a⁻¹ * a = 1

theorem mul_eq_of_eq_inv_mul (h : b = a⁻¹ * c) : a * b = c := by rw [h, mul_inv_cancel_left]

theorem mul_eq_of_eq_mul_inv (h : a = c * b⁻¹) : a * b = c := by simp [h]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
@[to_additive]
theorem inv_mul_eq_of_eq_mul (h : b = a * c) : a⁻¹ * b = c := by simp [h]

  rw [mul_inv_eq_one, mul_right_eq_self]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Unbundled.Basic

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Conj

theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/

  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩

    · congr

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

    (a : α) (l : List α) (b : α) :

  conv_lhs => unfold bidirectionalRec
  cases l with

  simp only [List.cons_append]
  dsimp only [← List.cons_append]
  suffices ∀ (ys init : List α) (hinit : init = ys) (last : α) (hlast : last = b),

      cast (congr_arg motive <| by simp [hinit, hlast])
        (cons_append a ys b (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append ys)) by
    rw [this (x :: xs) _ (by rw [dropLast_append_cons, dropLast_single, append_nil]) _ (by simp)]

  rintro ys init rfl last rfl
  rfl

        noncommProd t (comm.mono <| subset_of_le <| t.le_add_left s) := by

  rcases t with ⟨⟩
  simp

/-- An additive commutative monoid is an additive monoid with commutative `(+)`. -/

@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem CommMonoid.ext {M : Type*} ⦃m₁ m₂ : CommMonoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) : m₁ = m₂ :=
  CommMonoid.toMonoid_injective <| Monoid.ext h_mul

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
@[to_additive]
theorem mul_mul_mul_comm (a b c d : G) : a * b * (c * d) = a * c * (b * d) := by
  simp only [mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]

@[to_additive (attr := simp)]
lemma mul_of {A : Type*} [Monoid A] (a b : A) :
    @HMul.hMul (MonCat.of A) (MonCat.of A) (MonCat.of A) _ a b = a * b := rfl

/-- A commutative additive semigroup is a type with an associative commutative `(+)`. -/
@[ext]

@[to_additive]

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

--src: Mathlib.Data.List.Basic
@[simp]
theorem bidirectionalRec_cons_append {motive : List α → Sort*}
    (nil : motive []) (singleton : ∀ a : α, motive [a])
    (cons_append : ∀ (a : α) (l : List α) (b : α), motive l → motive (a :: (l ++ [b])))
    (a : α) (l : List α) (b : α) :
    bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append (a :: (l ++ [b])) =
      cons_append a l b (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append l) := by
  conv_lhs => unfold bidirectionalRec
  cases l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs =>
  simp only [List.cons_append]
  dsimp only [← List.cons_append]
  suffices ∀ (ys init : List α) (hinit : init = ys) (last : α) (hlast : last = b),
      (cons_append a init last
        (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append init)) =
      cast (congr_arg motive <| by simp [hinit, hlast])
        (cons_append a ys b (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append ys)) by
    rw [this (x :: xs) _ (by rw [dropLast_append_cons, dropLast_single, append_nil]) _ (by simp)]
    simp
  rintro ys init rfl last rfl
  rfl

theorem span.loop_eq_take_drop :
    ∀ l₁ l₂ : List α, span.loop p l₁ l₂ = (l₂.reverse ++ takeWhile p l₁, dropWhile p l₁)
  | [], l₂ => by simp [span.loop, takeWhile, dropWhile]
  | (a :: l), l₂ => by
    cases hp : p a <;> simp [hp, span.loop, span.loop_eq_take_drop, takeWhile, dropWhile]

/-- An `AddMonoid` is an `AddSemigroup` with an element `0` such that `0 + a = a + 0 = a`. -/
class AddMonoid (M : Type u) extends AddSemigroup M, AddZeroClass M where
  /-- Multiplication by a natural number.
  Set this to `nsmulRec` unless `Module` diamonds are possible. -/
  protected nsmul : ℕ → M → M
  /-- Multiplication by `(0 : ℕ)` gives `0`. -/
  protected nsmul_zero : ∀ x, nsmul 0 x = 0 := by intros; rfl
  /-- Multiplication by `(n + 1 : ℕ)` behaves as expected. -/
  protected nsmul_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x), nsmul (n + 1) x = nsmul n x + x := by intros; rfl

@[to_additive] lemma pow_mul_pow_eq_one : ∀ n, a * b = 1 → a ^ n * b ^ n = 1
  | 0, _ => by simp
  | n + 1, h =>
    calc
      a ^ n.succ * b ^ n.succ = a ^ n * a * (b * b ^ n) := by rw [pow_succ, pow_succ']
      _ = a ^ n * (a * b) * b ^ n := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = 1 := by simp [h, pow_mul_pow_eq_one]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter. -/
@[to_additive "Sometimes, an additive group is defined as a quotient of a monoid
  by an additive congruence relation.
  Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
  This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
  instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
  and `∀ x, c (f x + x) 0` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter."]
theorem map_of_mul_left_rel_one [Monoid M] (c : Con M)
    (f : M → M) (hf : ∀ x, c (f x * x) 1) {x y} (h : c x y) : c (f x) (f y) := by
  simp only [← Con.eq, coe_one, coe_mul] at *
  have hf' : ∀ x : M, (x : c.Quotient) * f x = 1 := fun x ↦
    calc
      (x : c.Quotient) * f x = f (f x) * f x * (x * f x) := by simp [hf]
      _ = f (f x) * (f x * x) * f x := by ac_rfl
      _ = 1 := by simp [hf]
  have : (⟨_, _, hf' x, hf x⟩ : c.Quotientˣ) = ⟨_, _, hf' y, hf y⟩ := Units.ext h
  exact congr_arg Units.inv this

theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄

    m₁ = m₂ := by

  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this

    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n

  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[to_additive] lemma left_inv_eq_right_inv (hba : b * a = 1) (hac : a * c = 1) : b = c := by

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter. -/
@[to_additive "Sometimes, an additive group is defined as a quotient of a monoid
  by an additive congruence relation.
  Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
  This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
  instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
  and `∀ x, c (f x + x) 0` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter."]
theorem map_of_mul_left_rel_one [Monoid M] (c : Con M)
    (f : M → M) (hf : ∀ x, c (f x * x) 1) {x y} (h : c x y) : c (f x) (f y) := by
  simp only [← Con.eq, coe_one, coe_mul] at *
  have hf' : ∀ x : M, (x : c.Quotient) * f x = 1 := fun x ↦
    calc
      (x : c.Quotient) * f x = f (f x) * f x * (x * f x) := by simp [hf]
      _ = f (f x) * (f x * x) * f x := by ac_rfl
      _ = 1 := by simp [hf]
  have : (⟨_, _, hf' x, hf x⟩ : c.Quotientˣ) = ⟨_, _, hf' y, hf y⟩ := Units.ext h
  exact congr_arg Units.inv this

lemma mul_of {A : Type*} [Monoid A] (a b : A) :

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.List
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_hom_rel (l : List ι) {r : M → N → Prop} {f : ι → M} {g : ι → N} (h₁ : r 1 1)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃i a b⦄, r a b → r (f i * a) (g i * b)) : r (l.map f).prod (l.map g).prod :=
  List.recOn l h₁ fun a l hl => by simp only [map_cons, prod_cons, h₂ hl]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

@[to_additive]
theorem npowRec_eq {M : Type*} [Semigroup M] [One M] (k : ℕ) (m : M) :
    npowRec (k + 1) m = 1 * npowRec' (k + 1) m := by
  induction k using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | ind k' ih =>
    match k' with
    | 0 => rfl
    | k + 1 =>
      rw [npowRec, npowRec'_succ k.succ_ne_zero, ← mul_assoc]
      congr
      simp [ih]

  /-- One is a left neutral element for multiplication -/

  protected mul_one : ∀ a : M, a * 1 = a

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter. -/
@[to_additive "Sometimes, an additive group is defined as a quotient of a monoid
  by an additive congruence relation.
  Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
  This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
  instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
  and `∀ x, c (f x + x) 0` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter."]
theorem map_of_mul_left_rel_one [Monoid M] (c : Con M)
    (f : M → M) (hf : ∀ x, c (f x * x) 1) {x y} (h : c x y) : c (f x) (f y) := by
  simp only [← Con.eq, coe_one, coe_mul] at *
  have hf' : ∀ x : M, (x : c.Quotient) * f x = 1 := fun x ↦
    calc
      (x : c.Quotient) * f x = f (f x) * f x * (x * f x) := by simp [hf]
      _ = f (f x) * (f x * x) * f x := by ac_rfl
      _ = 1 := by simp [hf]
  have : (⟨_, _, hf' x, hf x⟩ : c.Quotientˣ) = ⟨_, _, hf' y, hf y⟩ := Units.ext h
  exact congr_arg Units.inv this

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_hom_rel (l : List ι) {r : M → N → Prop} {f : ι → M} {g : ι → N} (h₁ : r 1 1)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃i a b⦄, r a b → r (f i * a) (g i * b)) : r (l.map f).prod (l.map g).prod :=
  List.recOn l h₁ fun a l hl => by simp only [map_cons, prod_cons, h₂ hl]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

/-- Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter. -/
@[to_additive "Sometimes, an additive group is defined as a quotient of a monoid
  by an additive congruence relation.
  Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
  This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
  instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
  and `∀ x, c (f x + x) 0` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter."]
theorem map_of_mul_left_rel_one [Monoid M] (c : Con M)
    (f : M → M) (hf : ∀ x, c (f x * x) 1) {x y} (h : c x y) : c (f x) (f y) := by
  simp only [← Con.eq, coe_one, coe_mul] at *
  have hf' : ∀ x : M, (x : c.Quotient) * f x = 1 := fun x ↦
    calc
      (x : c.Quotient) * f x = f (f x) * f x * (x * f x) := by simp [hf]
      _ = f (f x) * (f x * x) * f x := by ac_rfl
      _ = 1 := by simp [hf]
  have : (⟨_, _, hf' x, hf x⟩ : c.Quotientˣ) = ⟨_, _, hf' y, hf y⟩ := Units.ext h
  exact congr_arg Units.inv this

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

/-- A congruence relation on a type with an addition is an equivalence relation which
    preserves addition. -/
structure AddCon [Add M] extends Setoid M where
  /-- Additive congruence relations are closed under addition -/
  add' : ∀ {w x y z}, r w x → r y z → r (w + y) (x + z)

When possible, instead of parametrizing results over `(f : M →+ N)`,
you should parametrize over `(F : Type*) [AddMonoidHomClass F M N] (f : F)`.
When you extend this structure, make sure to extend `AddMonoidHomClass`.
-/

  ZeroHom M N, AddHom M N

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Unique
/-- `Unique α` expresses that `α` is a type with a unique term `default`.
This is implemented as a type, rather than a `Prop`-valued predicate,
for good definitional properties of the default term. -/
@[ext]
structure Unique (α : Sort u) extends Inhabited α where
  /-- In a `Unique` type, every term is equal to the default element (from `Inhabited`). -/
  uniq : ∀ a : α, a = default

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.AddConstMap.Basic
/-- A bundled map `f : G → H` such that `f (x + a) = f x + b` for all `x`.
One can think about `f` as a lift to `G` of a map between two `AddCircle`s. -/
structure AddConstMap (G H : Type*) [Add G] [Add H] (a : G) (b : H) where
  /-- The underlying function of an `AddConstMap`.
  Use automatic coercion to function instead. -/
  protected toFun : G → H
  /-- An `AddConstMap` satisfies `f (x + a) = f x + b`. Use `map_add_const` instead. -/
  map_add_const' (x : G) : toFun (x + a) = toFun x + b

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Ext
@[ext] theorem ext ⦃inst₁ inst₂ : NonUnitalSemiring R⦄
    (h_add : local_hAdd[R, inst₁] = local_hAdd[R, inst₂])
    (h_mul : local_hMul[R, inst₁] = local_hMul[R, inst₂]) :
    inst₁ = inst₂ :=
  toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring_injective <|
    NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring.ext h_add h_mul

/-- An `AddMonoid` is an `AddSemigroup` with an element `0` such that `0 + a = a + 0 = a`. -/
class AddMonoid (M : Type u) extends AddSemigroup M, AddZeroClass M where
  /-- Multiplication by a natural number.
  Set this to `nsmulRec` unless `Module` diamonds are possible. -/
  protected nsmul : ℕ → M → M
  /-- Multiplication by `(0 : ℕ)` gives `0`. -/
  protected nsmul_zero : ∀ x, nsmul 0 x = 0 := by intros; rfl
  /-- Multiplication by `(n + 1 : ℕ)` behaves as expected. -/
  protected nsmul_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x), nsmul (n + 1) x = nsmul n x + x := by intros; rfl

    (nil : motive []) (singleton : ∀ a : α, motive [a])

    (a : α) (l : List α) (b : α) :
    bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append (a :: (l ++ [b])) =

  conv_lhs => unfold bidirectionalRec
  cases l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs =>
  simp only [List.cons_append]
  dsimp only [← List.cons_append]
  suffices ∀ (ys init : List α) (hinit : init = ys) (last : α) (hlast : last = b),
      (cons_append a init last
        (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append init)) =
      cast (congr_arg motive <| by simp [hinit, hlast])
        (cons_append a ys b (bidirectionalRec nil singleton cons_append ys)) by
    rw [this (x :: xs) _ (by rw [dropLast_append_cons, dropLast_single, append_nil]) _ (by simp)]

  rintro ys init rfl last rfl
  rfl

  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f

      assumption
    · congr

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄

class Monoid (M : Type u) extends Semigroup M, MulOneClass M where
  /-- Raising to the power of a natural number. -/
  protected npow : ℕ → M → M := npowRecAuto
  /-- Raising to the power `(0 : ℕ)` gives `1`. -/
  protected npow_zero : ∀ x, npow 0 x = 1 := by intros; rfl
  /-- Raising to the power `(n + 1 : ℕ)` behaves as expected. -/
  protected npow_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x), npow (n + 1) x = npow n x * x := by intros; rfl

theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
/-- A `Group` is a `Monoid` with an operation `⁻¹` satisfying `a⁻¹ * a = 1`.
There is also a division operation `/` such that `a / b = a * b⁻¹`,
with a default so that `a / b = a * b⁻¹` holds by definition.
Use `Group.ofLeftAxioms` or `Group.ofRightAxioms` to define a group structure
on a type with the minimum proof obligations.
-/
class Group (G : Type u) extends DivInvMonoid G where
  protected inv_mul_cancel : ∀ a : G, a⁻¹ * a = 1

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias mul_left_inv := inv_mul_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias inv_mul_self := inv_mul_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias mul_right_inv := mul_inv_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  have h₁ : g₁.one = g₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (Monoid.ext h_mul)
  let f : @MonoidHom G G g₁.toMulOneClass g₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  exact
    Group.toDivInvMonoid_injective
      (DivInvMonoid.ext h_mul
        (funext <| @MonoidHom.map_inv G G g₁ g₂.toDivisionMonoid f))

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Equiv.Basic
/-- A multiplicative equivalence of groups preserves inversion. -/
@[to_additive "An additive equivalence of additive groups preserves negation."]
protected theorem map_inv [Group G] [DivisionMonoid H] (h : G ≃* H) (x : G) :
    h x⁻¹ = (h x)⁻¹ :=
  map_inv h x

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
@[to_additive]
theorem mul_eq_of_eq_mul_inv (h : a = c * b⁻¹) : a * b = c := by simp [h]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Units.Hom
/-- If two homomorphism from a group to a monoid are equal at `x`, then they are equal at `x⁻¹`. -/
@[to_additive
    "If two homomorphism from an additive group to an additive monoid are equal at `x`,
    then they are equal at `-x`."]
theorem eq_on_inv {F G M} [Group G] [Monoid M] [FunLike F G M] [MonoidHomClass F G M]
    (f g : F) {x : G} (h : f x = g x) : f x⁻¹ = g x⁻¹ :=
  (Group.isUnit x).eq_on_inv f g h

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[to_additive]
theorem eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left (h : a * b = 1) : a = b⁻¹ :=
  (inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_left h).symm

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Basic
@[to_additive existing (attr := simp)]
lemma mulLeft_one : Equiv.mulLeft (1 : α) = 1 := ext one_mul

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
/-- A `Group` is a `Monoid` with an operation `⁻¹` satisfying `a⁻¹ * a = 1`.
There is also a division operation `/` such that `a / b = a * b⁻¹`,
with a default so that `a / b = a * b⁻¹` holds by definition.
Use `Group.ofLeftAxioms` or `Group.ofRightAxioms` to define a group structure
on a type with the minimum proof obligations.
-/
class Group (G : Type u) extends DivInvMonoid G where
  protected inv_mul_cancel : ∀ a : G, a⁻¹ * a = 1

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias mul_left_inv := inv_mul_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias inv_mul_self := inv_mul_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias mul_right_inv := mul_inv_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  have h₁ : g₁.one = g₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (Monoid.ext h_mul)
  let f : @MonoidHom G G g₁.toMulOneClass g₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  exact
    Group.toDivInvMonoid_injective
      (DivInvMonoid.ext h_mul
        (funext <| @MonoidHom.map_inv G G g₁ g₂.toDivisionMonoid f))

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Equiv.Basic
/-- A multiplicative equivalence of groups preserves inversion. -/
@[to_additive "An additive equivalence of additive groups preserves negation."]
protected theorem map_inv [Group G] [DivisionMonoid H] (h : G ≃* H) (x : G) :
    h x⁻¹ = (h x)⁻¹ :=
  map_inv h x

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
@[to_additive]
theorem mul_eq_of_eq_mul_inv (h : a = c * b⁻¹) : a * b = c := by simp [h]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Units.Hom
/-- If two homomorphism from a group to a monoid are equal at `x`, then they are equal at `x⁻¹`. -/
@[to_additive
    "If two homomorphism from an additive group to an additive monoid are equal at `x`,
    then they are equal at `-x`."]
theorem eq_on_inv {F G M} [Group G] [Monoid M] [FunLike F G M] [MonoidHomClass F G M]
    (f g : F) {x : G} (h : f x = g x) : f x⁻¹ = g x⁻¹ :=
  (Group.isUnit x).eq_on_inv f g h

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
@[to_additive]
theorem eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left (h : a * b = 1) : a = b⁻¹ :=
  (inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_left h).symm

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Basic
@[to_additive existing (attr := simp)]
lemma mulLeft_one : Equiv.mulLeft (1 : α) = 1 := ext one_mul

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Equiv.Basic
/-- A multiplicative equivalence of groups preserves inversion. -/
@[to_additive "An additive equivalence of additive groups preserves negation."]
protected theorem map_inv [Group G] [DivisionMonoid H] (h : G ≃* H) (x : G) :
    h x⁻¹ = (h x)⁻¹ :=
  map_inv h x

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Group.ext {G : Type*} ⦃g₁ g₂ : Group G⦄ (h_mul : g₁.mul = g₂.mul) : g₁ = g₂ := by
  have h₁ : g₁.one = g₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) (Monoid.ext h_mul)
  let f : @MonoidHom G G g₁.toMulOneClass g₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  exact
    Group.toDivInvMonoid_injective
      (DivInvMonoid.ext h_mul
        (funext <| @MonoidHom.map_inv G G g₁ g₂.toDivisionMonoid f))

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
/-- A `Group` is a `Monoid` with an operation `⁻¹` satisfying `a⁻¹ * a = 1`.
There is also a division operation `/` such that `a / b = a * b⁻¹`,
with a default so that `a / b = a * b⁻¹` holds by definition.
Use `Group.ofLeftAxioms` or `Group.ofRightAxioms` to define a group structure
on a type with the minimum proof obligations.
-/
class Group (G : Type u) extends DivInvMonoid G where
  protected inv_mul_cancel : ∀ a : G, a⁻¹ * a = 1

@[deprecated (since := "2024-08-12")] alias mul_left_inv := inv_mul_cancel

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Units.Hom
/-- If two homomorphism from a group to a monoid are equal at `x`, then they are equal at `x⁻¹`. -/
@[to_additive
    "If two homomorphism from an additive group to an additive monoid are equal at `x`,
    then they are equal at `-x`."]
theorem eq_on_inv {F G M} [Group G] [Monoid M] [FunLike F G M] [MonoidHomClass F G M]
    (f g : F) {x : G} (h : f x = g x) : f x⁻¹ = g x⁻¹ :=
  (Group.isUnit x).eq_on_inv f g h

protected theorem map_inv [Group α] [DivisionMonoid β] (f : α →* β) (a : α) : f a⁻¹ = (f a)⁻¹ :=
  map_inv f _

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.EckmannHilton
/-- If a type carries two unital binary operations that distribute over each other,
then these operations are equal.
In fact, they give a commutative monoid structure, see `eckmann_hilton.CommMonoid`. -/
theorem mul : m₁ = m₂ := by
  funext a b
  calc
    m₁ a b = m₁ (m₂ a e₁) (m₂ e₁ b) := by
      { simp only [one h₁ h₂ distrib, h₁.left_id, h₁.right_id, h₂.left_id, h₂.right_id] }
    _ = m₂ a b := by simp only [distrib, h₁.left_id, h₁.right_id, h₂.left_id, h₂.right_id]

  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X

--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.NonemptyFinLinOrd
instance : SplitEpiCategory NonemptyFinLinOrd.{u} :=
  ⟨fun {X Y} f hf => by
    have H : ∀ y : Y, Nonempty (f ⁻¹' {y}) := by
      rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hf
      intro y
      exact Nonempty.intro ⟨(hf y).choose, (hf y).choose_spec⟩
    let φ : Y → X := fun y => (H y).some.1
    have hφ : ∀ y : Y, f (φ y) = y := fun y => (H y).some.2
    refine IsSplitEpi.mk' ⟨⟨φ, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    swap
    · ext b
      apply hφ
    · intro a b
      contrapose
      intro h
      simp only [not_le] at h ⊢
      suffices b ≤ a by
        apply lt_of_le_of_ne this
        rintro rfl
        exfalso
        simp at h
      have H : f (φ b) ≤ f (φ a) := f.monotone (le_of_lt h)
      simpa only [hφ] using H⟩

protected theorem id_traverse {σ α} (x : σ ⊕ α) :

--src: Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Basic
/-- A traversable functor is lawful if its `traverse` satisfies a
number of additional properties.  It must send `pure : α → Id α` to `pure`,
send the composition of applicative functors to the composition of the
`traverse` of each, send each function `f` to `fun x ↦ f <$> x`, and
satisfy a naturality condition with respect to applicative
transformations. -/
class LawfulTraversable (t : Type u → Type u) [Traversable t] extends LawfulFunctor t :
    Prop where
  /-- `traverse` plays well with `pure` of the identity monad -/
  id_traverse : ∀ {α} (x : t α), traverse (pure : α → Id α) x = x
  /-- `traverse` plays well with composition of applicative functors. -/
  comp_traverse :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G] {α β γ}
      (f : β → F γ) (g : α → G β) (x : t α),
      traverse (Functor.Comp.mk ∘ map f ∘ g) x = Comp.mk (map (traverse f) (traverse g x))
  /-- An axiom for `traverse` involving `pure : β → Id β`. -/
  traverse_eq_map_id : ∀ {α β} (f : α → β) (x : t α),
    traverse ((pure : β → Id β) ∘ f) x = id.mk (f <$> x)
  /-- The naturality axiom explaining how lawful traversable functors should play with
  lawful applicative functors. -/
  naturality :
    ∀ {F G} [Applicative F] [Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F] [LawfulApplicative G]
      (η : ApplicativeTransformation F G) {α β} (f : α → F β) (x : t α),
      η (traverse f x) = traverse (@η _ ∘ f) x

theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f

  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩

      assumption
    · congr

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

/-- A semigroup is a type with an associative `(*)`. -/
@[ext]
class Semigroup (G : Type u) extends Mul G where
  /-- Multiplication is associative -/
  protected mul_assoc : ∀ a b c : G, a * b * c = a * (b * c)

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Free

theorem lift_of_mul (x y) : lift f (of x * y) = f x * lift f y := by rw [map_mul, lift_of]

/-- Flipping arguments of monoid morphisms (`MonoidHom.flip`) as a monoid morphism. -/

      "Flipping arguments of additive monoid morphisms (`AddMonoidHom.flip`)
      as an additive monoid morphism."]
def flipHom {_ : MulOneClass M} {_ : MulOneClass N} {_ : CommMonoid P} :
    (M →* N →* P) →* N →* M →* P where
  toFun := MonoidHom.flip
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := rfl

/-- A `Monoid` is a `Semigroup` with an element `1` such that `1 * a = a * 1 = a`. -/

  /-- Raising to the power of a natural number. -/
  protected npow : ℕ → M → M := npowRecAuto
  /-- Raising to the power `(0 : ℕ)` gives `1`. -/
  protected npow_zero : ∀ x, npow 0 x = 1 := by intros; rfl
  /-- Raising to the power `(n + 1 : ℕ)` behaves as expected. -/
  protected npow_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x), npow (n + 1) x = npow n x * x := by intros; rfl

/-- A semigroup is a type with an associative `(*)`. -/
@[ext]
class Semigroup (G : Type u) extends Mul G where
  /-- Multiplication is associative -/
  protected mul_assoc : ∀ a b c : G, a * b * c = a * (b * c)

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Free
@[to_additive]
theorem lift_of_mul (x y) : lift f (of x * y) = f x * lift f y := by rw [map_mul, lift_of]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs
/-- A `Monoid` is a `Semigroup` with an element `1` such that `1 * a = a * 1 = a`. -/
@[to_additive]
class Monoid (M : Type u) extends Semigroup M, MulOneClass M where
  /-- Raising to the power of a natural number. -/
  protected npow : ℕ → M → M := npowRecAuto
  /-- Raising to the power `(0 : ℕ)` gives `1`. -/
  protected npow_zero : ∀ x, npow 0 x = 1 := by intros; rfl
  /-- Raising to the power `(n + 1 : ℕ)` behaves as expected. -/
  protected npow_succ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x), npow (n + 1) x = npow n x * x := by intros; rfl

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_hom₂ (l : List ι) (f : M → N → P) (hf : ∀ a b c d, f (a * b) (c * d) = f a c * f b d)

    (l.map fun i => f (f₁ i) (f₂ i)).prod = f (l.map f₁).prod (l.map f₂).prod := by
  rw [prod, prod, prod, foldr_map, foldr_map, foldr_map,
    ← l.foldr_hom₂ f _ _ (fun x y => f (f₁ x) (f₂ x) * y) _ _ (by simp [hf]), hf']

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem

  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f

  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩

      assumption
    · congr

@[to_additive (attr := simps tensorObj_as leftUnitor rightUnitor associator) Discrete.addMonoidal]
instance Discrete.monoidal : MonoidalCategory (Discrete M) where
  tensorUnit := Discrete.mk 1
  tensorObj X Y := Discrete.mk (X.as * Y.as)
  whiskerLeft X _ _ f := eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [eq_of_hom f])
  whiskerRight f X := eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [eq_of_hom f])
  tensorHom f g := eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [eq_of_hom f, eq_of_hom g])
  leftUnitor X := Discrete.eqToIso (one_mul X.as)
  rightUnitor X := Discrete.eqToIso (mul_one X.as)
  associator _ _ _ := Discrete.eqToIso (mul_assoc _ _ _)

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Ext
@[ext] theorem ext ⦃inst₁ inst₂ : Ring R⦄
    (h_add : local_hAdd[R, inst₁] = local_hAdd[R, inst₂])
    (h_mul : local_hMul[R, inst₁] = local_hMul[R, inst₂]) :
    inst₁ = inst₂ := by
  -- Show that enough substructures are equal.
  have h₁ : inst₁.toSemiring = inst₂.toSemiring := by
    ext : 1 <;> assumption
  have h₂ : inst₁.toNonAssocRing = inst₂.toNonAssocRing := by
    ext : 1 <;> assumption
  /- We prove that the `SubNegMonoid`s are equal because they are one
  field away from `Sub` and `Neg`, enabling use of `injection`. -/
  have h₃ : (inst₁.toAddCommGroup).toAddGroup.toSubNegMonoid
            = (inst₂.toAddCommGroup).toAddGroup.toSubNegMonoid :=
    congrArg (@AddGroup.toSubNegMonoid R) <| by ext : 1; exact h_add
  -- Split into fields and prove they are equal using the above.
  cases inst₁; cases inst₂
  congr <;> solve | injection h₂ | injection h₃

  protected toFun : M → N

  protected map_one' : toFun 1 = 1

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by
    intro s t h
    suffices cast hU (g s).2 = cast hU (g t).2 by
      simp only [g, cast_cast, cast_eq] at this
      assumption
    · congr
  exact cantor_injective g hg

--src: Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Equiv
/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an
injective coercion to bijections between `α` and `β`.
Note that this does not directly extend `FunLike`, nor take `FunLike` as a parameter,
so we can state `coe_injective'` in a nicer way.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the isomorphism (or equivalence) typeclasses,
such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....
-/
class EquivLike (E : Sort*) (α β : outParam (Sort*)) where
  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`

@[ext]
theorem ext ⦃f g : r ≃r s⦄ (h : ∀ x, f x = g x) : f = g :=
  DFunLike.ext f g h

theorem Hom.inductionOn {motive : {X Y : F C} → (X ⟶ Y) → Prop} {X Y : F C} (t : X ⟶ Y)
    (id : (X : F C) → motive (�� X))
    (α_hom : (X Y Z : F C) → motive (α_ X Y Z).hom)
    (α_inv : (X Y Z : F C) → motive (α_ X Y Z).inv)
    (l_hom : (X : F C) → motive (λ_ X).hom)
    (l_inv : (X : F C) → motive (λ_ X).inv)
    (ρ_hom : (X : F C) → motive (ρ_ X).hom)
    (ρ_inv : (X : F C) → motive (ρ_ X).inv)
    (comp : {X Y Z : F C} → (f : X ⟶ Y) → (g : Y ⟶ Z) → motive f → motive g → motive (f ≫ g))
    (whiskerLeft : (X : F C) → {Y Z : F C} → (f : Y ⟶ Z) → motive f → motive (X ◁ f))
    (whiskerRight : {X Y : F C} → (f : X ⟶ Y) → (Z : F C) → motive f → motive (f ▷ Z)) :
    motive t := by
  apply Quotient.inductionOn
  intro f
  induction f with
  | id X => exact id X
  | α_hom X Y Z => exact α_hom X Y Z
  | α_inv X Y Z => exact α_inv X Y Z
  | l_hom X => exact l_hom X
  | l_inv X => exact l_inv X
  | ρ_hom X => exact ρ_hom X
  | ρ_inv X => exact ρ_inv X
  | comp f g hf hg => exact comp _ _ (hf ⟦f⟧) (hg ⟦g⟧)
  | whiskerLeft X f hf => exact whiskerLeft X _ (hf ⟦f⟧)
  | whiskerRight f X hf => exact whiskerRight _ X (hf ⟦f⟧)
  | @tensor W X Y Z f g hf hg =>
      have : homMk f ⊗ homMk g = homMk f ▷ X ≫ Y ◁ homMk g :=
        Quotient.sound (HomEquiv.tensorHom_def f g)
      change motive (homMk f ⊗ homMk g)
      rw [this]
      exact comp _ _ (whiskerRight _ _ (hf ⟦f⟧)) (whiskerLeft _ _ (hg ⟦g⟧))

/-- The equivalence that is part of the universal property of the pushout. A hom out of
the pushout is just a morphism out of all groups in the pushout that satisfies a commutativity
condition. -/
@[simps]
def homEquiv :
    (PushoutI φ →* K) ≃ { f : (Π i, G i →* K) × (H →* K) // ∀ i, (f.1 i).comp (φ i) = f.2 } :=
  { toFun := fun f => ⟨(fun i => f.comp (of i), f.comp (base φ)),
      fun i => by rw [MonoidHom.comp_assoc, of_comp_eq_base]⟩
    invFun := fun f => lift f.1.1 f.1.2 f.2,
    left_inv := fun _ => hom_ext (by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff])
      (by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff])
    right_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ => by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff, funext_iff] }

theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by

  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this

    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩

--src: Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Equiv
/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an
injective coercion to bijections between `α` and `β`.
Note that this does not directly extend `FunLike`, nor take `FunLike` as a parameter,
so we can state `coe_injective'` in a nicer way.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the isomorphism (or equivalence) typeclasses,
such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....
-/
class EquivLike (E : Sort*) (α β : outParam (Sort*)) where
  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`

@[ext]

    (α_hom : (X Y Z : F C) → motive (α_ X Y Z).hom)
    (α_inv : (X Y Z : F C) → motive (α_ X Y Z).inv)
    (l_hom : (X : F C) → motive (λ_ X).hom)
    (l_inv : (X : F C) → motive (λ_ X).inv)
    (ρ_hom : (X : F C) → motive (ρ_ X).hom)
    (ρ_inv : (X : F C) → motive (ρ_ X).inv)
    (comp : {X Y Z : F C} → (f : X ⟶ Y) → (g : Y ⟶ Z) → motive f → motive g → motive (f ≫ g))
    (whiskerLeft : (X : F C) → {Y Z : F C} → (f : Y ⟶ Z) → motive f → motive (X ◁ f))
    (whiskerRight : {X Y : F C} → (f : X ⟶ Y) → (Z : F C) → motive f → motive (f ▷ Z)) :
    motive t := by
  apply Quotient.inductionOn
  intro f
  induction f with
  | id X => exact id X
  | α_hom X Y Z => exact α_hom X Y Z
  | α_inv X Y Z => exact α_inv X Y Z
  | l_hom X => exact l_hom X
  | l_inv X => exact l_inv X
  | ρ_hom X => exact ρ_hom X
  | ρ_inv X => exact ρ_inv X
  | comp f g hf hg => exact comp _ _ (hf ⟦f⟧) (hg ⟦g⟧)
  | whiskerLeft X f hf => exact whiskerLeft X _ (hf ⟦f⟧)
  | whiskerRight f X hf => exact whiskerRight _ X (hf ⟦f⟧)

      rw [this]

/-- `OneHom M N` is the type of functions `M → N` that preserve one.
When possible, instead of parametrizing results over `(f : OneHom M N)`,
you should parametrize over `(F : Type*) [OneHomClass F M N] (f : F)`.
When you extend this structure, make sure to also extend `OneHomClass`.
-/
@[to_additive]
structure OneHom (M : Type*) (N : Type*) [One M] [One N] where
  /-- The underlying function -/
  protected toFun : M → N
  /-- The proposition that the function preserves 1 -/
  protected map_one' : toFun 1 = 1

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.PushoutI
/-- The equivalence that is part of the universal property of the pushout. A hom out of
the pushout is just a morphism out of all groups in the pushout that satisfies a commutativity
condition. -/
@[simps]
def homEquiv :
    (PushoutI φ →* K) ≃ { f : (Π i, G i →* K) × (H →* K) // ∀ i, (f.1 i).comp (φ i) = f.2 } :=
  { toFun := fun f => ⟨(fun i => f.comp (of i), f.comp (base φ)),
      fun i => by rw [MonoidHom.comp_assoc, of_comp_eq_base]⟩
    invFun := fun f => lift f.1.1 f.1.2 f.2,
    left_inv := fun _ => hom_ext (by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff])
      (by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff])
    right_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ => by simp [DFunLike.ext_iff, funext_iff] }

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Ext
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem Monoid.ext {M : Type u} ⦃m₁ m₂ : Monoid M⦄
    (h_mul : (letI := m₁; HMul.hMul : M → M → M) = (letI := m₂; HMul.hMul : M → M → M)) :
    m₁ = m₂ := by
  have : m₁.toMulOneClass = m₂.toMulOneClass := MulOneClass.ext h_mul
  have h₁ : m₁.one = m₂.one := congr_arg (·.one) this
  let f : @MonoidHom M M m₁.toMulOneClass m₂.toMulOneClass :=
    @MonoidHom.mk _ _ (_) _ (@OneHom.mk _ _ (_) _ id h₁)
      (fun x y => congr_fun (congr_fun h_mul x) y)
  have : m₁.npow = m₂.npow := by
    ext n x
    exact @MonoidHom.map_pow M M m₁ m₂ f x n
  rcases m₁ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  rcases m₂ with @⟨@⟨⟨_⟩⟩, ⟨_⟩⟩
  congr

/-- Extensionality rule for congruence relations. -/
@[to_additive (attr := ext) "Extensionality rule for additive congruence relations."]
theorem ext {c d : Con M} (H : ∀ x y, c x y ↔ d x y) : c = d :=
  ext' <| by ext; apply H

/-- There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
  demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean. -/
theorem not_surjective_Type {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f := by
  intro hf
  let T : Type max u v := Sigma f
  cases hf (Set T) with | intro U hU =>
  let g : Set T → T := fun s ↦ ⟨U, cast hU.symm s⟩
  have hg : Injective g := by

--src: Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Equiv
/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an
injective coercion to bijections between `α` and `β`.
Note that this does not directly extend `FunLike`, nor take `FunLike` as a parameter,
so we can state `coe_injective'` in a nicer way.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the isomorphism (or equivalence) typeclasses,
such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....
-/
class EquivLike (E : Sort*) (α β : outParam (Sort*)) where
  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`

inductive StAct (k : K)

--src: Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Equiv
/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an
injective coercion to bijections between `α` and `β`.
Note that this does not directly extend `FunLike`, nor take `FunLike` as a parameter,
so we can state `coe_injective'` in a nicer way.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the isomorphism (or equivalence) typeclasses,
such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....
-/
class EquivLike (E : Sort*) (α β : outParam (Sort*)) where
  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`

--src: Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Equiv
/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an
injective coercion to bijections between `α` and `β`.
Note that this does not directly extend `FunLike`, nor take `FunLike` as a parameter,
so we can state `coe_injective'` in a nicer way.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the isomorphism (or equivalence) typeclasses,
such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....
-/
class EquivLike (E : Sort*) (α β : outParam (Sort*)) where
  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Hom.Monoid
@[to_additive (attr := ext)]
theorem ext (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) : f = g :=
  DFunLike.ext f g h

--src: Mathlib.Order.Hom.Bounded
theorem copy_eq (f : TopHom α β) (f' : α → β) (h : f' = f) : f.copy f' h = f :=
  DFunLike.ext' h

/-- A stack action is a command that interacts with the top of a stack. Our default position
is at the bottom of all the stacks, so we have to hold on to this action while going to the end
to modify the stack. -/
inductive StAct (k : K)
  | push : (σ → Γ k) → StAct k
  | peek : (σ → Option (Γ k) → σ) → StAct k
  | pop : (σ → Option (Γ k) → σ) → StAct k

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Hom.Monoid
/-- `OrderMonoidWithZeroHom α β` is the type of functions `α → β` that preserve
the `MonoidWithZero` structure.
`OrderMonoidWithZeroHom` is also used for group homomorphisms.
When possible, instead of parametrizing results over `(f : α →+ β)`,
you should parameterize over
`(F : Type*) [FunLike F M N] [MonoidWithZeroHomClass F M N] [OrderHomClass F M N] (f : F)`. -/

  [MulZeroOneClass β] extends α →*₀ β where
  /-- An `OrderMonoidWithZeroHom` is a monotone function. -/
  monotone' : Monotone toFun

/-- The class `EquivLike E α β` expresses that terms of type `E` have an

such as `ZeroEquivClass`, `MulEquivClass`, `MonoidEquivClass`, ....

  /-- The coercion to a function in the forward direction. -/
  coe : E → α → β
  /-- The coercion to a function in the backwards direction. -/
  inv : E → β → α
  /-- The coercions are left inverses. -/
  left_inv : ∀ e, Function.LeftInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The coercions are right inverses. -/
  right_inv : ∀ e, Function.RightInverse (inv e) (coe e)
  /-- The two coercions to functions are jointly injective. -/
  coe_injective' : ∀ e g, coe e = coe g → inv e = inv g → e = g
  -- This is mathematically equivalent to either of the coercions to functions being injective, but
  -- the `inv` hypothesis makes this easier to prove with `congr'`
